results.mechanism: On a tray-icon click, StatusBarEntry::OnMessage calls popupFrame->GetNearestWidget() (SystemStatusBar.cpp:188) on a not-yet-shown menu popup; it returns null and trips the nightly-only MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(widget) at line 189. GetNearestWidget resolves a widget via the frame's view hierarchy, and bug 1933181 'Stop using nsView for popups' removes exactly that popup nsView, so the popup no longer resolves to a widget here. Bugzilla confirms it: crash bug 1994855 is regressed_by 1933181. CAVEAT: the literal hash 068ddb3652ea is a test-manifest-only follow-up ('two tests I missed', Linux/Wayland .toml skip-ifs) and cannot itself crash — it is a proxy for bug 1933181, whose actual popup/nsView code is the cause.

Changeset 91bfadad8e0a replaced the graceful 'if (type == Unsupported) return NS_ERROR_FAILURE' guard in WakeLockTopic::UninhibitScreensaver() with MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(mWakeLockType != Unsupported) (line 897) and split the type into a per-topic mWakeLockType copied from the global type in SendInhibit(). When the global wake-lock type has degraded to Unsupported at runtime, that value propagates into the topic's mWakeLockType, so the next uninhibit — previously a silent no-op — now trips the new diagnostic assert and crashes on nightly. Blame, build-date, and Bugzilla regressed_by (bug 2027756 regressed_by 2023381) all confirm it.

The MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(!foundInPendingQ) fires when ProcessNewTransaction→CheckTransInPendingQueue→RemoveTransFromConnEntry finds a transaction being processed as 'new' already sitting in its ConnectionEntry's pending queue. Enabling HEv3 (racing/re-dispatch across entries whose hash keys shift with IP family/H3) breaks that invariant and is a Bugzilla-confirmed regressor of this signature (bug 2041239 regressed_by 2039555) — but only for builds from ~2026-05-19/24 onward.
results.refutation: The crash build (buildid 20260514203426 = rev 2c58ea699acf, dated 2026-05-14) predates the candidate 50641796ae6e (landed 2026-05-19) by 5 days, so the change is not in the binary. It is also a pure nightly-default pref-flip of network.http.happy_eyeballs_enabled (false→@IS_NIGHTLY_BUILD@) plus a test-only WPT .ini edit — no product code — so with HEv3 off-by-default in this build it can have no effect; crash-stats first-seen (2026-05-24) likewise postdates the build.

results.mechanism: Changeset b5d6bfc12f00 (bug 1966326) vendors the app-services Rust logins component and wires desktop/Thunderbird's password-manager storage (storage-rust.sys.mjs) to build the store at startup via createLoginStoreWithNssKeymanager, which opens the logins SQLite DB with LoginStore::new. At the crash build that Result was .unwrap()ed instead of propagated (tip now uses `?`), so a corrupt/invalid DB returning SQLITE_NOTADB ('file is not a database') panics -> RustMozCrash startup crash. Fixed by propagating the error as ApiResult.

A themed <input type=range> is painted as an image (SVG/-moz-element callback) into a content-process DrawTargetRecording; Theme::PaintRange draws the thumb shadow via PaintCircleShadow, which calls CreateSimilarDrawTargetForFilter for the blur, the recording DT's CanCreateSimilarDrawTarget returns false, and the content-process branch hits MOZ_CRASH. Bug 1971450 removed the internal range/progress/meter appearance values and made nsRangeFrame paint atomically through the theme (DisplayBorderBackgroundOutline + 'don't paint children'), newly routing the recorded range through the pre-existing PaintCircleShadow filter-target landmine.

The vendored llama.cpp is compiled unconditionally with -mavx2 on x86_64 (third_party/llama.cpp/moz.build), and ggml-threading.cpp's global `std::mutex ggml_critical_section_mutex` has a dynamic initializer the CRT runs at DLL attach, before any CPU-feature gate. On an x86_64 CPU lacking AVX2, the VEX-encoded instruction in the AVX2-compiled inlined std::mutex constructor faults with an illegal instruction at startup (thread 0), matching sibling bug 1986900 'invalid instruction'. Introduced by the sibling vendoring changeset 47e0ba3acc33, not by the candidate.
results.refutation: Candidate 010afe1fcabb ('Patch out static ctors') modifies only llama-arch.cpp (converting its global std::map tables to lazy std::call_once accessors) and adds static-ctors.patch. It does not touch ggml-threading.cpp, the ggml_critical_section_mutex, the DLL-init path, or the AVX2 moz.build flags that emit the illegal instruction, so it cannot produce this fault. It is a fix-direction change for the same static-ctor bug class that simply missed the ggml-threading mutex; the actual regressor is the sibling changeset 47e0ba3acc33 (the 2025-08-23 'Vendor llama.cpp' commit that added both the file and the AVX2 build config).

results.mechanism: Bug 1980056 pins mozjemalloc's logical page size to 4KiB while the OS page stays 16KiB on Apple-Silicon macOS, and 'pt 2' removes the sub-page size class (reworking NUM_SMALL_CLASSES/gMaxBinClass/bin+run page-count mapping). The purge path (Purge→PurgeLoop→FindDirtyPages/ScanForFirstDirtyPage) walks mPageMap and counts dirty pages at gPagesPerRealPage granularity; an inconsistency introduced by that rework makes the dirty-page accounting/run-walk fault — either a MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT (e.g. mDirtyNPages==0 at the crash line) or a wild-pointer deref of a run reconstructed from a mangled page-map word.

Bug 543435 landed three changesets on 2025-11-24 (the build day) that introduced nsDocShell::ShouldDoInitialAboutBlankSyncLoad and the initial-about:blank sync-load path reached via BrowserChild::RecvLoadURL→LoadURI→InternalLoad→DoURILoad; that new code dereferences load-time state (mDocumentViewer/its document, mBrowsingContext, or aURI) that can be null on some loads, faulting. This is a fresh 543435 regression, later tracked as bug 2013289.
results.refutation: Changeset 3c99a43d1d94 is bug 2003244 ('Don't crash when failing to initialize docshell'), authored 2026-01-06 — ~6 weeks AFTER this build (2025-11-24). The build tree (rev 87bd2ca15e2a) still has the pre-change 'NS_ENSURE_TRUE(Initialize(...), NS_ERROR_FAILURE)' at nsDocShell.cpp:449, so the change is verifiably absent from the build; it is also a defensive anti-crash fix that does not touch ShouldDoInitialAboutBlankSyncLoad or its call path.

results.mechanism: Rust panic in wgpu_hal::dx12::Adapter::expose during D3D12 feature/shader-model detection: the '_ => unreachable!()' at adapter.rs:322 fires when CheckFeatureSupport(D3D12_FEATURE_SHADER_MODEL) returns a HighestShaderModel outside the enumerated arms (matches moz_crash_reason 'entered unreachable code'), and/or a .unwrap() on CheckFeatureSupport/GetDesc2 returning an error HRESULT (matches the core::result::unwrap_failed token). Bug 2005294 (wgpu bump to upstream 3f02781b) is the Bugzilla-confirmed regressor of the exact-signature topcrash bug 2007754.
results.refutation: The specific node 75de582fbae9 is NOT the causative change: it modifies only supply-chain/audits.toml (a cargo-vet audit sign-off for the 'ron' crate, 0.11.0->0.12.0), ships no executable code, and doesn't touch wgpu-hal. Bug 2005294 never modified adapter.rs (file_history + blame), so the regression is off-stack within the wgpu/naga upstream bump; the causative re-vendor is a sibling changeset in the same push, not this audit leaf. Corroboration holds at the bug/push level, not for this exact changeset.

results.mechanism: Bug 1851992 (this changeset) added an off-main-thread OnDataFinished notification: on Nightly (pref defaulted @IS_NIGHTLY_BUILD@) HttpChannelChild::SendOnDataFinished runs on the retargeted ODATarget thread and calls OnDataFinished down through nsHTTPCompressConv/InterceptFailedOnStop into nsDocumentOpenInfo::OnDataFinished, which AddRefs its m_targetStreamListener; when that listener is a JS-implemented (nsXPCWrappedJS) nsIStreamListener, the AddRef off-main-thread trips MOZ_RELEASE_ASSERT(NS_IsMainThread()). The entire call chain is new with this bug, and Bugzilla records bug 1992512 (this exact crash) as regressed_by 1851992.

0b168428809a rewrote PendingTransactionQueue::CancelAllTransactions to gather raw nsHttpTransaction* pointers, then Clear() the urgent queue and pending table (dropping the PendingTransactionInfo strong RefPtrs), and only afterward call trans->Close(). When the queue held the last reference, Clear() frees the transaction, so Close()'s mReqHeaderBuf.Truncate() at line 1768 decrements a StringBuffer refcount through a dangling this — a use-after-free crashing in the atomic fetch_sub.

During WebCodecs VideoEncoder reconfigure, the on-the-fly reconfigure rejects and the Then-lambda calls mAgent->Drain()->...->SetState(); the EncoderAgent (mAgent/mEncoder) has been reset/destroyed in flight, so SetState dereferences a near-null 'this'/member (MOZ_ASSERTs are compiled out in the opt nightly, so line 431 is an inlining artifact, not an assertion). This is a confirmed regression of bug 1749047 (bug 2016493 regressed_by 1749047).

In TexUnpackSurface::BlitSd, glFramebufferTexture2D attaches the destination WebGL texture to a scratch FBO and MOZ_ALWAYS_TRUE(!err) asserts no GL error; on Windows ANGLE/D3D (gpu process) the driver rejects the color attachment for some target/level/format and the assert fires. The real regressor is bug 1972649's changeset c11e7594c36d ('Add fast-path for Accelerated Canvas2D to WebGL copies'), which re-routed this blit path — Bugzilla bug 1979112 is regressed_by 1972649.
results.refutation: The candidate node 47d8d7840ccb is NOT bug 1972649 — it is bug 1971400, a Fenix Android UI-test revert (all 22 files under mobile/android/fenix/, androidTest/test code) that touches no graphics/WebGL/canvas code, is not compiled into desktop Firefox, and cannot run in the Windows GPU process where the crash happens. Blame of the crashing lines 895-904/851 shows bug 1769747 and bug 1972649 (c11e7594c36d), never 47d8d7840ccb. The node is almost certainly just the build-tip revision (same 2025-07-22 date as build 20250722093426); the true culprit changeset for bug 1972649 is c11e7594c36d.

results.mechanism: Changeset c640bfafa636 (bug 1979075) adds fog_control::init::collect_directory_info, called nightly-only at FOG startup. It does an is_dir() check then fs::read_dir(&dir_path).unwrap() / entry.unwrap() / entry.metadata().unwrap() on the actively-mutated FOG dirs (db/events/pending_pings). A TOCTOU race — the directory or a file disappearing between the check and the read/stat — returns Err(Os{code:2,NotFound}), which the unwrap turns into the panic matching this exact signature.

Bug 1851870 (a3a13413c12c) made GMP teardown asynchronous (SendShutdown()->Then, the frame #3/#4 promise callbacks that call DeleteProcess) and added a terminal GMPState::Closed with a `case Closed: break;` fall-through to mProcess->Delete(), while also changing ActorDestroy to set Closed and call DeleteProcess. This lets DeleteProcess reach mProcess->Delete() twice — once via abnormal-shutdown/ActorDestroy and once via the deferred Shutdown promise resolve/reject — so the second call runs Delete() on an already-null/freed mProcess and faults on the `mDeletedCallback = aCallback` nsCOMPtr assignment (frame #0's nsITimer is identical-code-folding of the nsCOMPtr assign helper; GMPProcessParent has no timer, only mDeletedCallback at offset 464).

Changeset 6828a42b3856 introduced the Maybe<StripRule> mStripOnShareGlobal field and rewrote ShouldStripParam to dereference it unconditionally via mStripOnShareGlobal.ref() at URLQueryStringStripper.cpp:410, replacing the old graceful mStripOnShareMap.Get("*") bool path. When ShouldStripParam runs (via CanStripForShare) while the strip-on-share list hasn't yet delivered an isGlobal:true rule — async not-yet-populated, reset at line 238, or a list with no global rule — the Maybe is Nothing and ref()'s MOZ_RELEASE_ASSERT(isSome()) fires. The isSome() guard at line 413 sits after the deref, so it cannot prevent it.

On the V4L2 HW-decode path, CreateImageV4L2 reinterpret-casts mFrame->data[0] to AVDRMFrameDescriptor and FFmpegDescToVA reads aDesc.layers[0].planes[0].pitch/offset; the SEGV_MAPERR (arm64/rdd) is a read of an invalid/unmapped/malformed DRM descriptor from FFmpeg's V4L2 decoder. Bug 2021722 is the confirmed regressor (bug 2046425), but via its decoder-refactor changeset, not this one.
results.refutation: This is a changeset-level (not bug-level) refutation. 009ece72f8eb touches only prefs/packaging/configure/GfxInfo-vulkantest and DMABufFormats/DMABufSurface (EGL modifiers, semaphore-fd, CreateTextureViaCopy); it does NOT modify FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp/FFmpegVideoFramePool.cpp nor the acquisition of AVDRMFrameDescriptor from mFrame->data[0], and its DMABuf changes run downstream of (after) the crashing FFmpegDescToVA read, so its diff cannot produce this fault. It also landed 2026-04-29, ~31 days before the signature's first-seen buildid 20260530, pointing at a later sibling changeset of bug 2021722 (the FFmpegVideoDecoder Vulkan/`&drmDesc` refactor) as the real mechanism.

results.mechanism: OnChannelConnected posts a main-thread runnable capturing liveToken=mLiveToken but then checks *mLiveToken (i.e. this->mLiveToken) instead of the captured copy; if the GPUProcessHost is destroyed before the runnable runs, reading this->mLiveToken/mLaunchPhase through the dangling this dereferences jemalloc-poisoned memory → poison UAF at GPUProcessHost.cpp:123. This matches bug 2002422's csectype-uaf/sec-high 'Poison crash' classification.

WebGPU content drives wgpu-hal's D3D12 backend to call ID3D12Device::CreateCommandSignature; the D3D12 runtime's CCommandSignature::FinalConstruct copies the caller-supplied D3D12_INDIRECT_ARGUMENT_DESC array into a std::vector, and a malformed/oversized descriptor from the updated wgpu dx12 backend faults during that resize inside the Intel driver. Bug 1991551 bumps the vendored wgpu rev, changing exactly that backend.

Bug 1964605 (m-c node f73e0c41c92c, autoland sibling cb4f6a9c197c; blame-confirmed present in the crash build) changed worker AbortSignal.timeout from WorkerPrivate::SetTimeout to inserting directly into the worker global's TimeoutManager, so those timeouts are now run by TimeoutManager::RunTimeout; when such a handler's synchronous abort dispatch causes ClearAllTimeouts() (RunTimeoutHandler returns cleared=true) while a timeout remains in that manager, MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(!HasTimeouts()) at TimeoutManager.cpp:956 fires. Bugzilla independently records this exact assert (bug 1978585) as regressed_by 1964605.

At EventDispatcher.cpp:495 the copy-ctor `nsCOMPtr<EventTarget> firstTarget = aVisitor.mEvent->mTarget` (nsCOMPtr.h:384-390) dereferences aVisitor.mEvent; a null or freed WidgetEvent makes the read of mTarget fault (SIGSEGV/SEGV_MAPERR). 100% Linux/parent-process/startup matches a GTK widget-level regressor dispatching an event with a stale/freed event object.
results.refutation: The candidate changeset 2a8d531e3aab is the automated 'apply code formatting via Lando' commit (bug 672103): its entire diff is whitespace around '+' operators in nsWindow::ConstrainSizeWithScale, byte-identical object code, touching only widget/gtk/nsWindow.cpp with no relation to WidgetEvent lifetime — it cannot introduce the null/dangling aVisitor.mEvent. IMPORTANT: this is 'right bug, wrong changeset' — the PARENT bug 1992198 IS the confirmed regressor (Bugzilla: crash bug 1998188 with this exact signature is regressed_by 1992198, topcrash-startup); the real cause is 1992198's substantive 'don't cache scaled coordinates' sibling changeset, not this formatting commit.

results.mechanism: In an OfflineAudioContext, MediaTrackGraphImpl::Process() renders block-by-block across [mProcessedTime, mStateComputedTime); each block, idling Web Audio nodes call ScheduleCheckForInactive -> RunMessageAfterProcessing, appending to mFrontMessageQueue[0].mMessages, which is only drained AFTER Process() returns. When the offline per-iteration interval (mEndTime - mStateComputedTime, later clamped in the fix) is unbounded, one Process() iterates over millions of blocks and grows that array to ~59M UniquePtr entries -> 454 MiB infallible Realloc -> OOM. Bug 1503132 reworked exactly this offline-graph thread lifecycle and mEndTime semantics.

Bug 1661106's screen-capture feature creates a MozPromise (call-site 'RecvRequestScreenPixels') stored in WebRenderBridgeParent's Maybe<ScreenPixelsRequest>; when that request is reset/overwritten/destroyed at teardown without first resolving, rejecting, or disconnecting the promise, ~ThenValueBase::AssertIsDead() MOZ_CRASHes in ~ScreenPixelsRequest. Bugzilla confirms crash bug 2014723 is regressed_by bug 1661106.
results.refutation: Changeset 13d768fdb8a4 is a Lando auto-format commit that only reformats widget/android/moz.build (rewriting a sorted([...]) call's bracket placement); classes_with_WrapForJNI and the generated JNI headers are identical, so it has zero runtime/C++ effect and touches none of the crashing code. The real regressor is a different C++ changeset within the same bug 1661106 — right bug, wrong changeset.

results.mechanism: The change made ParseHTML/parseHTMLUnsafe sanitize the Document node instead of its <html> root element, so SanitizeChildren now visits <html> as a direct child. With config replaceWithChildrenElements:["html"] (the <false>/non-default-config path), the unwrap branch computes parent = child->GetParent(), which returns nullptr because <html>'s parent is the Document (not an nsIContent); it then calls parent->InsertBefore(...) on null, reaching EnsurePreInsertionValidity1 -> IsDocument() with this==null, faulting near address 0. Matches the stack exactly and is newly reachable only after this change.

SIGSEGV/SEGV_MAPERR null/near-null deref in the AVDRMFrameDescriptor overload of VideoFramePool::GetVideoFrameSurface (FFmpegVideoFramePool.cpp ~621), reached only via FFmpegVideoDecoder::CreateImageVulkan — the Linux/GTK hardware Vulkan video-decode path in the rdd process, which exists solely because of bug 2021722. crash-stats (100% rdd/Linux/amd64/SEGV_MAPERR) and Bugzilla (bug 2047016 for this exact signature is regressed_by 2021722) both confirm it.

On a click/keyselect of the Windows system-status-bar tray icon, StatusBarEntry::OnMessage resolves the <xul:menu>'s nsMenuPopupFrame but popupFrame->GetNearestWidget() returns null, so MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(widget) at SystemStatusBar.cpp:189 fires — a popup frame/view→widget association gap, i.e. a Layout/Widget popup-plumbing fault.
results.refutation: Candidate 0057bb3d85dd (bug 1966674, DOM: Navigation) modifies only docshell/base/nsDocShell.cpp::HandleSameDocumentNavigation (Navigation API session-history state on same-document fragment navigation); there is no path from that to a null nearest-widget on a chrome XUL popup frame in the Windows tray handler. The existing RESOLVED-FIXED bug for this exact signature (1994855) is regressed_by 1933181 'Stop using nsView for popups' (Core::Layout), which directly reworked popup view/widget association — the true mechanism.

results.mechanism: In the Windows sandbox broker, a child's NtOpenFile IPC drives FilesystemDispatcher::EvalPolicy → PolicyProcessor/PolicyOpcode::Evaluate → OpcodeEval<OP_NUMBER_MATCH>, which calls param->Get() (policy_engine_opcodes.cc:140); ParameterSet::Get faults at policy_engine_params.h:67 reading real_type_ off a malformed/bad ParameterSet built for policy evaluation. Independently attributed to sandbox-policy regressor bug 1996225 by two FIXED bugs (1997854, 2009140).
results.refutation: 06270780f139 is an automated 'No Bug - Bumping Mobile l10n changesets ... DONTBUILD' commit that modifies only mobile/locales/l10n-changesets.json (a Fenix/Android localization pointer). It compiles no code, targets the mobile product, and touches nothing in the Windows-only sandbox policy engine, so it cannot produce a fault in sandbox::ParameterSet::Get. The signature's real regressor is bug 1996225 (a sandbox policy change).

results.mechanism: On Windows, WebRender's wr_thread_pool_new (gfx/webrender_bindings/src/bindings.rs:1141-1159) does rayon ThreadPoolBuilder::...build().unwrap(); under thread/memory exhaustion the OS refuses new threads (Win error 8), build() returns Err(ThreadPoolBuildError{IOError=OutOfMemory}), and the mandatory .unwrap() panics into MOZ_Crash. It's a resource-exhaustion crash whose real cause is prior thread proliferation (per known bug 2006934: DisableGPUProcess + many RemoteBackbuffer threads, regressed_by bug 2001152's async compositor init).
results.refutation: Candidate 060a0a7be5c9 (bug 1979049, Layout: Text and Fonts) only reverses a FontFaceRecord array and iterates it back-to-front in FontFaceSetDocumentImpl.cpp — pure main-thread C++ font bookkeeping with no thread creation, no rayon, and no GPU/compositor path. It cannot cause an OS 'cannot create thread' failure in a WebRender/Stylo rayon pool build; the signature's known regressor is bug 2001152 (Graphics/RemoteBackbuffer), a different bug and subsystem, and this change is a perf fix that reduces work rather than adding thread/memory pressure.

results.mechanism: IsChainValid passes the NSSCertDBTrustDomain member mDistrustAfterTime as the out-param to IsDistrustedCertificateChain, which calls distrustAfterTimeOut.emplace() (NSSCertDBTrustDomain.cpp:1356) without first reset()-ing it. During recursive/backtracking cert path building (two BuildForward/PathBuildingStep::Check frames) IsChainValid runs more than once on the same instance; the second emplace hits an already-Some Maybe and MOZ_RELEASE_ASSERT(!isSome()) fires.
results.refutation: Candidate 000b97a486f3 (bug 1972159, 'Enable Compose Homepage by Default') touches only Fenix/Android Kotlin homepage UI files (BookmarksViewHolder.kt, SessionControlAdapter.kt, SessionControlView.kt); the crash is in shared C++ NSS/PSM cert verification in desktop Firefox with no code or data path to it. Blame shows the crashing emplace at line 1356 was introduced by dc509eab3ed7 / bug 1953221, which is exactly the regressor already recorded on the pre-existing signature bug 1981271.

results.mechanism: RangeBasedTextDirectiveCreator assumes a range-based text directive has a non-empty end context term; mEndContent came back empty, tripping MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(!mEndContent.IsEmpty()) at TextDirectiveCreator.cpp:388. It is reached synchronously from JS via FragmentDirective.createTextDirectiveForSelection (the copy-link-to-highlight feature). The assert and the invariant were introduced by bug 1978976 (changeset 5266c5cc9daa), which Bugzilla already lists as the regressor of the matching bug 1979588.
results.refutation: Candidate 00b0ff261a15 (bug 1978398) is a Firefox-for-Android Fenix Kotlin toolbar/tabstrip UI change (only mobile/android/fenix/*.kt, gating add-tab/tab-counter buttons via a showActionButtons flag). It shares no code, state, or data flow with the C++ DOM text-directive path in dom/base/TextDirectiveCreator.cpp and cannot influence whether mEndContent is empty. Blame and bug 1979588's regressed_by both attribute this signature to bug 1978976, not 1978398, whose only regression (1981160) is an Android toolbar-UI issue.

results.mechanism: In RangeBasedTextDirectiveCreator::CollectContextTerms, FindBlockBoundaryInRange<Right>(*mRange) returns Some so the code enters the branch, but the paired FindBlockBoundaryInRange<Left>(*mRange) returns Nothing, violating the left/right symmetry invariant and firing MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(lastBlockBoundaryInRange.isSome()) — a logic bug in the text-fragment block-boundary scanner (block introduced by bug 1957557; per Bugzilla the exact signature is bug 1979474, regressed_by 1976480).
results.refutation: Candidate 003b4c7a0320 (bug 1978141, Core::DOM: Notifications) only modifies dom/notification/NotificationUtils.cpp, adding a null-check on notificationStorage in GetStoredNotificationsForScope. It touches neither dom/base/TextDirectiveCreator.cpp nor TextDirectiveUtil.h, and no frame on the crashing stack (FragmentDirective::CreateTextDirectiveForSelection → CollectContextTerms) relates to notification storage; there is no data/control-flow path connecting the two subsystems.

results.mechanism: Deliberate MOZ_CRASH in the content process: Theme::PaintRange -> PaintCircleShadow requests a blur-filter draw target sized from the range thumb's box rect (A8), and DrawTargetRecording::CreateSimilarDrawTargetForFilter aborts because mFinalDT->CanCreateSimilarDrawTarget returns false for that size/format on the blob-recording backend (surface too large/invalid, amplified by the enclosing scaled SVG-image draw).
results.refutation: 065dae4a196b (bug 1971135) is a behavior-preserving refactor of CSS anchor-position resolution plumbing (AnchorPosResolutionParams::From) touching only layout/{base,generic,style}; it passes the identical frame and StyleDisplay()->mPosition as before and touches none of the crash path (gfx/2d/DrawTargetRecording.cpp, widget/Theme.cpp, filter/SVG-image code). The identical MOZ_CRASH (bug 1981495) is regressed_by bug 1971450 'Remove internal appearance values for progress/meter/range', which actually changed the PaintRange path in this stack — a different, mechanistically plausible bug that is merely adjacent to the candidate in the same mid-June window.

results.mechanism: Vendored native ggml/llama.cpp (bug 1971158) is built with CPU instructions (AVX/AVX2 family) absent on the affected CPUs; at DLL load the CRT runs the dynamic initializer _GLOBAL__sub_I_ggml_threading.cpp to construct the global std::mutex ggml_critical_section_mutex, and the first unsupported instruction in that init code raises an illegal-instruction fault, surfacing as a crash in std::_Mutex_base::_Mutex_base during dllmain_crt_process_attach.
results.refutation: Candidate 065bdfa00df5 (bug 1985662, 'Sub out Page Buddy Ai request functionality') is pure JS/CSS/test — PageAssist actors and a MOCK fetchAiResponse (// TODO: Call AI API here). It adds no native code, does not vendor/build llama.cpp, changes no /arch or compiler flags, and never invokes a native inference path, so it cannot produce a native static-init illegal-instruction crash in ggml. Both signature bugs (1987003, 1986900) are regressed by bug 1971158 'Vendor llama.cpp', not by 1985662.

results.mechanism: Enabling -webkit-fill-available (and/or intrinsic keywords) let a StyleSize that is neither 'auto', stretch-like, nor a LengthPercentage flow into ComputeBSizeValueHandlingStretch during reflow; its final branch calls aSize.AsLengthPercentage(), tripping MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(IsLengthPercentage()) while computing an inline-size with block-size as percentage basis.
results.refutation: Candidate 00f984fb8fba/bug 1982004 is a Firefox-for-Android Kotlin change to a bottom-sheet menu animation (MenuDialogFragment.kt), gating it on Android SDK version; it touches no C++/Gecko layout, style, or CSS-value code and cannot influence which size values reach AsLengthPercentage. The signature's own fix bugs (1989368, 1990034) are both regressed_by bug 1988938 ('Enable -webkit-fill-available'), a different bug in Core::CSS Parsing and Computation, which matches the mechanism.

results.mechanism: MOZ_ALWAYS_TRUE(isNodeContainedInRange) at ContentIterator.cpp:1245 fires because RangeUtils::IsNodeContainedInRange returned Nothing() — CompareNodeToRange failed since the Selection's range fed to ContentSubtreeIterator was non-positioned or had unset/invalid start/end boundaries (a DOM: Selection range-boundary-validity bug, matching bug 1979463 regressed_by 1975990).
results.refutation: 739cd5fd1d92 (bug 1969305, Layout: Positioned) is a purely mechanical refactor of CSS max-width/max-height resolution (passing AnchorPosResolutionParams instead of its .mPosition field); it touches no dom/base range/selection code and cannot leave a range's boundaries unset/invalid. The authoritative regressor for this exact signature+line is DOM: Selection bug 1975990 (per bug 1979463's regressed_by), whose summary is literally the boundary IsSetAndValid condition that makes IsNodeContainedInRange return Nothing.

results.mechanism: A scrollable/form-control subtree (see ScrollContainerFrame in the stack, and bug 1873301 giving buttons overflow:scroll/auto) is fragmented inside a multicol; CreateContinuingFrame has no case for that frame type, so it falls through to MOZ_CRASH("unexpected frame type") at line 8053.
results.refutation: 8394a65c9c82/bug 1977267 only removes the pref layout.css.align-content.blocks.enabled, which was already value:true (default-on on Nightly), so it is a behavioral no-op on this channel and cannot introduce a new crash. The change is orthogonal to frame-type dispatch, adds no new fragmentable frame type, and has no regressions linked; the exact crash line 8053 is tracked by bug 1978487, regressed_by bug 1873301 (button overflow:scroll), which matches the ScrollContainerFrame in the stack.

results.mechanism: BlitSd builds a temporary FBO and attaches the destination WebGL texture as COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 via fFramebufferTexture2D; when that texture isn't a valid/renderable color attachment on the Windows driver (bad internal format or texture/level completeness), the attach errors or the FBO is incomplete and the MOZ_ALWAYS_TRUE checks (lines 900/904) MOZ_CRASH. Windows-only, GPU-process WebGL upload fast path.
results.refutation: Changeset 003367bc2366 modifies only taskcluster/scripts/builder/build-android.sh (an Android CI build script) for a Firefox-for-Android 'About' string bug (1976521). It changes no C++/build input for Windows desktop and is never run in desktop builds, so it cannot affect the Windows GPU-process WebGL BlitSd code. The known regressor for this exact signature is a different bug (1972649, per bug 1979112, Core::Graphics::CanvasWebGL).

results.mechanism: SIGSEGV/SEGV_MAPERR dereferencing aVisitor.mEvent (a WidgetEvent* const documented 'Never nullptr') at EventDispatcher.cpp:495 to read its mTarget nsCOMPtr (offset 80); the WidgetEvent pointer is null (fault ~0x50) or dangling (use-after-free / lifetime-invariant violation) when it reaches HandleEventTargetChain on desktop-Linux parent-process event dispatch.
results.refutation: Changeset 06270780f139 is an automated 'Bumping Mobile l10n changesets ... DONTBUILD CLOSED TREE' commit that modifies only mobile/locales/l10n-changesets.json (a localization-string repo revision). It contains no C++/JS/Rust or build code, is explicitly DONTBUILD, and targets mobile/Fenix — whereas the crash is desktop-Linux parent-process C++ in EventDispatcher. There is no data path from an l10n string revision to a null/dangling WidgetEvent* in HandleEventTargetChain.

results.mechanism: RangeBasedTextDirectiveCreator computes mFirstWordOfStartContent = Substring(mStartContent, 0, mStartWordEndDistances[0]) in CollectContextTermWordBoundaryDistances; when the selection's start content begins with an immediate word boundary (leading whitespace/punctuation/non-word or SVG/plain-text content) the first word-end distance is 0, producing an empty first word, which trips MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(!mFirstWordOfStartContent.IsEmpty()) in FindAllMatchingCandidates. Reached at runtime via JS FragmentDirective.createTextDirectiveForSelection.
results.refutation: The candidate diff modifies only taskcluster/scripts/builder/build-android.sh (adds a `mach build pre-export export` step) — no C++/runtime code and nothing in dom/. Bug 1976521 is an Android build-system fix (Firefox for Android; regressed_by 1960103, Gradle/Android build), which cannot affect a DOM string computed from selection contents at runtime. The actual crash bug for this exact signature, 1978976 (Core::DOM:Navigation), is independently attributed to a different regressor chain (1978235/1976473) inside the text-directive code.

results.mechanism: AutoClonedRangeArray::FirstRangeRef() unconditionally returns mRanges[0]; during HandleDeleteNonCollapsedRanges block-joining, WhiteSpaceVisibilityKeeper::MergeFirstLine...IntoDescendantLeftBlockElement -> AutoMoveOneLineHandler::Prepare calls FirstRangeRef() on an AutoClonedRangeArray whose mRanges is empty (moz_crash_reason ElementAt(aIndex=0, aLength=0)), tripping the nsTArray bounds MOZ_CRASH — an editor-side invariant violation in the white-space/delete-join path.
results.refutation: Bug 1971135 is a behavior-preserving Layout:Positioned refactor (anchor-size AnchorPosResolutionParams::From() helpers) confined to layout/base|generic|style; it touches no editor/, nsRange, Selection, or AutoClonedRangeArray code and is nowhere on the crash's call path, so it cannot make the range array empty. The exact signature's known regressor is editor bug 1951038 (legacy white-space normalizer removal), which lies directly on the crash stack (WhiteSpaceVisibilityKeeper frames), per the identical-signature VERIFIED-FIXED bug 1978481.

results.mechanism: Iterator-invalidation UAF in DataChannelConnection::CloseAll's STS lambda: the range-for over the live std::set mPending (line 1373/1376) calls FinishClose_s, which does mPending.erase(aChannel) (line 1325) on the current element, invalidating the loop iterator and dropping the set's strong ref; the next ++/deref yields a freed/garbage DataChannel*, whose RefPtr construction at line 1322 faults in AddRef's atomic fetch_add.
results.refutation: Blame at the crash build rev attributes every crashing line (FinishClose/FinishClose_s/CloseAll lambda incl. the mPending loop) to a59073be1506 = bug 1927886 ('Rewrite close/closing logic'), which Bugzilla records as the confirmed regressor of crash bug 1979072 (regressed_by 1927886). Candidate 679d65db1681/bug 1727116 only converts MediaTransportHandler's sigslot signaling to MediaEventProducer; it touches DataChannel.cpp only in the packet/transport-signal wiring, wrote none of the close-path lines, and the fault is a self-contained single-thread erase-during-iteration on mPending that is independent of the signaling change.

results.mechanism: Use-after-free: PromiseJobRunnable::Run reads a stale/recycled `callback = CallbackPreserveColor()` JSObject* and passes it to xpc::NativeGlobal → GetNonCCWObjectGlobal → IsProxy, which dereferences the freed object's shape (shadow/Shape.h:57). Introduced by bug 1960461's 'merge PromiseJobRunnable+PromiseJobCallback and recycle one instance' change.
results.refutation: Candidate 152a0c0ed6c4 (bug 1961816) only changes microtask-checkpoint *scheduling* (mMicroTaskRecursionDepth uint32_t→Maybe, the depth-0/widget-event guard); its diff never touches CallbackPreserveColor/mCallback/runnable recycling — the crashing data flow. Blame attributes the crashing line 224 to bug 1960461, and Bugzilla independently records 1980730 (this signature, csectype-uaf) as regressed_by 1960461, not 1961816. The crash path is a worklet module-load checkpoint, not the macOS widget-event path 1961816 altered.

results.mechanism: BrowsingContext::DidSet(IDX_LanguageOverride, nsCString&&) PreOrderWalks the BC subtree and calls windowContext->GetInnerWindow() without null-checking windowContext = aBrowsingContext->GetCurrentWindowContext(); that getter can return nullptr, so GetInnerWindow() runs with this==nullptr and reads the mWindowGlobalChild WeakPtr at a small offset off null, faulting in WeakPtr::operator bool()/RefPtr<WeakReference>::get() (RefPtr.h:314).
results.refutation: Changeset 000fb32879d2 (bug 1570400) modifies only 5 build/CI/test files (build/moz.build, a Python smoketest + manifest under build/test/python/, and two taskcluster source-test yml/kind entries). It adds no shipping C++ and touches nothing in docshell/ or mfbt/, so it cannot change the runtime behavior of BrowsingContext::DidSet / WindowContext::GetInnerWindow / WeakPtr::operator bool. It landed 2025-08-19, one day before the build — proximity only.

results.mechanism: Enabling -webkit-fill-available (bug 1988938) let a table row's computed block-size hold a StyleSize variant that is neither auto nor a length-percentage; ReflowInput::InitConstraints (ReflowInput.cpp:2399) takes its else-branch and calls StyleGenericSize::AsLengthPercentage() on that value, tripping the IsLengthPercentage() tag assertion at ServoStyleConsts.h:13997.
results.refutation: Candidate 00f984fb8fba (bug 1982004, Firefox for Android :: Design System and Theming) only edits Fenix Kotlin UI code (MenuDialogFragment.kt — a BottomSheet menu animation gated behind an Android SDK-version check). That Android application-UI layer has no path to Gecko's C++ table-reflow/Servo StyleSize code, so it cannot produce this tagged-union mismatch. Bugzilla attributes both existing bugs for this signature (1989368, 1990034) to bug 1988938 (enable -webkit-fill-available), not to 1982004.

results.mechanism: In RunMicroTask, the embedder pulls the engine's host-defined-data object from a microtask job and release-asserts it has class sHostDefinedDataClass; the object handed back has a different JSClass, so the microtask/host-defined-data plumbing returned something the embedder never installed. Consistent with a default-on engine change to microtask handling (bug 1997192, 'Enable JS MicroTaskQueue by default'), which Bugzilla lists as the regressor of the signature bug 2000305.
results.refutation: 0185dfbbc41d (bug 1967968) is a pure build-system/taskcluster change adding a Terser JS-minifier toolchain in CI (no C++, JS-engine, DOM-binding, or microtask code touched) and was backed out; it cannot alter the content-process runtime host-defined-data JSClass contract. The crash is independently attributed on Bugzilla to bug 1997192 (Enable JS MicroTaskQueue by default), and bug 1967968's own recorded regressions are 2009742/2022530, not 2000305. The candidate merely landed one day before the first-seen build, i.e. it is in the window but off-mechanism.

results.mechanism: In WaylandSurface::GetNextTransactionLocked the surface's mBufferTransactions list still contains a BufferTransaction whose IsDeleted() is true, so the MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT(!t->IsDeleted()) at WaylandSurface.cpp:1109 fires (and dereferencing the stale/freed transaction can also surface as the InvalidArrayIndex_CRASH|ElementAt bounds fault) — a use-after-delete/lifecycle bug in Linux Wayland buffer-transaction bookkeeping (Core::Widget:Gtk; the fixed instance bug 1979106 was regressed by bug 1978207).
results.refutation: Changeset 003367bc2366 (bug 1976521) modifies only taskcluster/scripts/builder/build-android.sh — an Android-only build script — adding a `mach build pre-export export` step. It changes no runtime C++, and widget/gtk Wayland code is neither built nor run on Android, so it cannot alter BufferTransaction lifecycle or mBufferTransactions and cannot produce this desktop-Linux crash.

results.mechanism: Out-of-bounds/invalid read while walking the in-memory ELF PT_NOTE note-header chain (line 369 deref of note_header->n_type). The loop only tests note_header < section_end but advances by NOTE_PADDING(n_namesz)+NOTE_PADDING(n_descsz) read from the mapped image, and section_length comes from dlpi_phdr p_memsz, so a malformed/oversized note segment in a loaded .so (Android linker/libsentry/eglsubAndroid) walks the pointer into unmapped memory during SharedLibraryInfo::GetInfoForSelf shared-library enumeration.
results.refutation: 003b4c7a0320 (bug 1978141) only adds a null-check on notificationStorage in dom/notification/NotificationUtils.cpp (Core :: DOM: Notifications). It shares no call path, data, or memory with the mozglue baseprofiler ELF note-walker, and it removes a crash rather than introducing one — it cannot make a PT_NOTE segment malformed. The signature's own bug 1981751 (Gecko Profiler, Android 5.1) attributes it to a different regressor, 1773313.

results.mechanism: A Selection spanning a shadow-DOM/flat-tree boundary makes AbstractRange::GetClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor(AllowRangeCrossShadowBoundary::Yes) return a null/stale node; RegisterSelection->RegisterClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor then dereferences it via MarkDescendants(*aNode)->IsMaybeSelected()->GetBoolFlag reading mBoolFlags at/near null -> EXC_BAD_ACCESS. This is the flattened-tree selection path (added by bug 1932150) and its ComparePoints/TreeKind regressor (bug 2012637/2012797 per Bugzilla), reached from a JS Selection.extend() call.
results.refutation: Changeset 00481fa83f5b is test-only: its whole diff is 9 print-reftest HTML pairs plus a reftest.list entry, no production code. Reftests run in CI and don't ship, whereas the 37 crashes are real-user content-process crashes across macOS 15/26/27 and Win11. Bug 1965847 is also a printing (nsPrintJob) change while the crash stack contains no printing frames (it is JS Selection.extend()->RegisterSelection). This exact signature's bugs (2022877, 2052026) are regressed_by 2012637/2012797, and blame attributes the crashing flattened-tree path to bug 1932150 - none of these is 1965847.

results.mechanism: Third-party endpoint-security software Trellix (ex-FireEye/McAfee) injects fcagff.dll into Firefox and inline-hooks the file-read path; its detour code (frames #7 @0x71a20fff trampoline → fcagff.dll@... ) faults and RaiseException tears down thread 0 under nsFileStreamBase::Read→PR_Read. This is an environmental/third-party defect (confirmed by bug 2006941: same signature, 32-bit builds + Trellix), not a Firefox-code regression.
results.refutation: Changeset 0067817ee3f7 (bug 1771789) is a WebRTC getUserMedia/getDisplayMedia media-track-clone *constraints* change, and its actual diff is test-only (a WPT .ini metadata file and a mediacapture-streams .https.html test) — no shipping code. It cannot alter nsFileStreamBase::Read, NSPR FileRead, or anything a Trellix file-read hook wraps; no media/getUserMedia frame appears on the stack, and the crash executes entirely inside injected third-party DLL code.

results.mechanism: With javascript.options.use_js_microtask_queue enabled (bug 1997192), PerformMicroTaskCheckPoint dequeues microtasks into a JS::Rooted<MustConsumeMicroTask>; a filled task reaches the wrapper's destructor without being consumed (mMicroTask not undefined), tripping MOZ_CRASH("Didn't consume MicroTask"). It's a consume-logic bug in the newly-enabled JS microtask-queue path, not in Rooting/GC init.
results.refutation: 55652ba60d45 only added `constexpr` to SafelyInitialized<T>::create() (line 226) and removed an #ifdef that gated solely a compile-time static_assert; the runtime body `return T();` sits OUTSIDE the #ifdef and is unchanged on all platforms (blame: body predates the patch). create() therefore value-initializes MustConsumeMicroTask to an undefined/consumed state identically before and after, so the change cannot make a task go unconsumed. The known regressor of this exact signature is bug 1997192 ("Enable JS MicroTaskQueue by default"), per regressed_by on bug 2003956.

results.mechanism: Null-pointer dereference of mTransaction at nsHttpChannel.cpp:8018: ProcessLNAActions() (entered from OnStartRequest when mStatus==NS_ERROR_LOCAL_NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED) unconditionally calls mTransaction->GetTargetIPAddressSpace() with no null guard, and mTransaction can be null by that point (cache-served/torn-down/raced channel). This code was added by bug 1960627 (changeset 1d0091c56339), the Local Network Access feature — which is exactly what the pre-existing crash bug 1980035 lists as regressed_by.
results.refutation: Candidate 1901f0e0dd78 (bug 1872780) only removes the layout.css.size-adjust.enabled CSS/@font-face pref, touching FontFace.webidl, FontFaceImpl.cpp, StaticPrefList.yaml and font_face.rs — no networking/HTTP/transaction/LNA code and nothing on the OnStartRequest→ProcessLNAActions path, so it cannot null out mTransaction or produce this fault.
